scenarios.title: Reconstruct the Linden evidence record
scenarios.context: Use the first stage of the PE08 public lesson. All facts are fictional. Build the first version before applying later changes. These are optional written self-review tasks; no peer or instructor response is provided. Numerical answers are public worked calculations, not protected assessment keys.
facts: Casey Linden requests a consumer-purpose closed-end first-lien principal-residence purchase loan for possible Fannie Mae delivery. Ordinary TRID and general ATR coverage are stipulated, not inferred from the property alone.

All six TRID elements arrive Monday September 14, 2026 at 14:00. The lender is open for substantially all business functions Monday–Friday, no relevant holiday applies, and the application remains pending. Initial LE receipt in person occurs Thursday September 17.

Price and initially estimated value are $450,000; requested loan is $360,000 at fixed 6.00%, 360 end-of-month payments, monthly compounding. No mortgage insurance is included under the stipulated initial structure.

Application income is $9,000: $6,600 salary, $1,400 pension and $1,000 expected bonus. Employer records show $3,300 semimonthly. Jules accepts salary and pension after individual review, but the bonus lacks the required support.
Other included payments are $420 vehicle, $90 revolving and $240 student debt, all accepted case inputs. Taxes $450, insurance $125 and dues $100 are additional monthly housing costs.

B1 has a $122,000 ending balance after the $12,000 earnest deposit cleared; complete pages are received. The source of an $18,000 transfer is unresolved. An assistant asks to reject the pension because pension recipients should not take new mortgages.
The fictional company screen is 45.00% DTI. It is not a federal or universal Fannie Mae limit and does not establish QM status.

tasks.prompt: Write five source-to-decision rows for the application event, salary, pension, bonus and transfer. Distinguish reported, received, reviewed and accepted; state the next evidence and reviewer for each open issue.
rubric: Preserve September 14 as the supplied application event
Use $8,000 as accepted income while retaining the $9,000 reported figure
Do not describe a complete bank statement as acceptance of the transfer source
Ask a proportionate source question through an authorized channel
Avoid real identifiers and allegations unsupported by the facts
tasks.rationale: A useful source map explains what a record establishes and what it leaves unresolved. It does not conceal a difference between an application and accepted evidence.

tasks.prompt: Explain why the initial LE date, the seven-business-day LE wait and an ECOA completed-application determination are separate questions. Show the September counts.
rubric: Initial LE count is September 15, 16 and 17 under the creditor-business-day definition
LE waiting-period count is September 18, 19, 21, 22, 23, 24 and 25
Do not add verification or a signature as a seventh TRID element
Identify creditor procedures, actual information and reasonable diligence for the Regulation B inquiry
tasks.rationale: The same file can contain different statutory triggers. A familiar portal status cannot unify them.

tasks.prompt: Write a three-to-five-sentence recommendation addressing the pension instruction, bonus and open transfer. Name the source type for each conclusion.
rubric: Individual pension evidence supports the supplied acceptance
The unsupported bonus is excluded for evidence reasons
The pension stereotype should be corrected and routed to compliance
Explain why this is an analysis of actual treatment, not a finding from a statistical disparity
Do not promise credit approval
tasks.rationale: The current Regulation B income protection and its July 2026 scope must be applied accurately. Acceptance of one documented source does not validate every other claimed source.

scenarios.title: Reconcile value product and late debt
scenarios.context: Continue the same fictional file using the dated replacement facts below. Keep the earlier evidence version visible. Your recommendation is a statement for the authorized reviewer, not permission to approve. All payment mechanics have explicit public derivations.
facts: On September 21 the accepted appraised value is $440,000 while the price remains $450,000. Apply the ordinary Fannie Mae purchase LTV denominator; no exception applies. For the unchanged $360,000 loan, the raw ratio is 81.8181818…%, mathematically rounded to 81.82% for this classroom display. The Fannie Mae guide instead truncates to 81.81%, then rounds up to 82% for delivery. Casey requests a $352,000 fixed loan at 6.00% over 360 payments, giving exactly 80.00% mathematically and 80% for delivery.
The revised fixed P&I is $2,110.42. Housing add-ons remain $675. Accepted income remains $8,000; other existing debts remain $750.

On September 25 B2 establishes the $18,000 deposit as an unsecured personal installment loan with $380 monthly payment and more than ten payments left. Casey previously called it a gift. No fraud finding is supplied.
Before payoff, B1 still shows $122,000. The other $104,000 is stipulated eligible. The company DTI screen remains 45.00%; there is no authorized exception decision.

On September 29 at 09:00 Jules accepts reliable evidence of actual full payoff, no remaining payment and a current $104,000 account balance after the $18,000 outflow, with no other cash movement or payoff charge. Jules accepts debt exclusion only after the required full analysis.

For a separate product illustration on $352,000, an ARM starts at 5.25% for 60 monthly payments, then adjusts annually. First and later adjustment caps are 2 percentage points; lifetime increase cap is 5 points; floor is 2.75%; margin is 2.75%. At the first reset the hypothetical index is 4.50%, producing 7.25%. Use theoretical unrounded amortization, remaining term 300 months. This alternative has not been found eligible.

rubric: Use $440,000 rather than $450,000 as the specified denominator
Distinguish the 81.82% classroom mathematical display from truncation to 81.81% and rounding up to the 82% Fannie Mae delivery ratio
Show the original and revised loan amounts
Contribution rises from $90,000 to $98,000
Route collateral questions without requesting a target value
Do not invent a contract cancellation right or program approval
tasks.rationale: A value change has linked payment and cash consequences; a correct LTV alone does not resolve the file.

tasks.prompt: Write separate September 25 and September 29 records showing DTI, eligible cash, evidence and decision owner. Explain why both versions show $104,000 usable cash.

tasks.prompt: Explain the fixed and ARM payment paths to Casey in four sentences. Include the first-reset scenario, additional housing costs and one material limit of the illustration.

scenarios.title: Defend the closing hold
scenarios.context: Continue with the corrected $352,000 fixed loan. This case separates financial accuracy, disclosure compliance and title acceptance. Use a concise decision and consumer message. No real transfer, loan release or external communication occurs.
facts: Initial LE receipt in person was September 17; CD receipt in person was September 24. No holiday, waiver or restart applies to those original waits. The appointment is September 29.

Initial gross closing charges $9,800 comprise a $900 lender fee, a $1,500 ten-percent aggregate and $7,400 other charges. Actual amounts are $950, $1,690 and $7,400. Ren stipulates the categories, performed services, valid baseline and no permitted baseline revision.

Northbank implements a valid $90 lender-paid correction. Price contribution $98,000, prepaids/escrow $4,200, earnest credit $12,000 and seller credit $5,000 are unchanged. All credits are stipulated lawful, reviewed and fully usable; no other adjustments apply.
Ren finds the corrected APR accurate, no disclosed product change and no added prepayment penalty. By September 29 at 10:00 Ren has accepted the actual required corrected-CD receipt evidence.

Jules has accepted the stated debt payoff and $104,000 assets. The title team has not accepted seller-lien resolution evidence. A seller email says it was paid. Company procedure requires the title disposition and the release officer’s actual release decision.
A referral partner offers to absorb $90 in exchange for future settlement referrals. A separate email changes the wire account. Neither has been approved or independently verified.

scenarios.title: Separate refinance and servicing clocks
scenarios.context: This is a separate hypothetical later transaction using the source rules checked September 30, 2026. It does not prove the main purchase closed or that current evidence will be sufficient later. All coverage and dates needed for the worked calculation are supplied.
facts: Casey is now stipulated to own and occupy the home. A different creditor provides a consumer-purpose refinance subject to the ordinary rescission rule. No exemption or waiver applies, every required consumer is identified, and all pre-consummation disclosure waits were separately satisfied.

Consummation and all required consumers’ receipt of the rescission notice and material disclosures occur Monday October 5, 2026. No relevant holiday affects the October 6–8 count. The creditor must also be reasonably satisfied no consumer rescinded.

New principal $360,000. Old loan principal statement $351,000. Payoff quote $352,250 good through October 9. Closing charges $5,600 and prepaids/escrow $1,650 are paid from proceeds. No other uses or adjustments apply.

For the delayed-receipt variation, the quote expressly adds $58.60 per calendar day after October 9 through receipt on October 13; four added days apply, with no other charges. This contract convention differs from the rescission business-day rule.

For a separate servicing illustration on the lesson fixed structure, annual taxes rise from $5,400 to $5,760 and insurance from $1,500 to $1,620. All other amounts are unchanged; assume no shortage or surplus adjustment. The $100 association dues remain a separate household obligation.
A covered servicing transfer later occurs. The borrower asks whether transfer protection means no payment is due; no actual late-payment facts or account notice are supplied.
